title: A Supplier’s Guide to Amazon's Packaging and Labeling Requirements
summary: Master Amazon packaging and labeling rules. Learn how Vendor Central (1P) and Seller Central (3P) standards prevent costly chargebacks and shortages.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


The operational divide between Vendor Central (1P) and Seller Central (3P) packaging and labeling requirements


-


High-frequency failure points across prep, barcodes, polybags, and ASNs that trigger chargebacks


-


How to establish a repeatable pre-shipment workflow that protects supplier margins and strengthens dispute recovery


When suppliers experience recurring deductions, inventory rejections, or receiving delays on Amazon, the root cause is rarely an ignorance of the retailer's guidelines. Amazon publishes extensive manuals detailing box dimensions, pallet heights, and barcode specifications. The true challenge lies in translating those static requirements into a repeatable warehouse prep, labeling, and electronic data interchange (EDI) workflow. Without operational discipline, minor preparation gaps quickly multiply into automated non-compliance fees, prep charges, and shortage claims that erode profit margins.


Maintaining compliance has become even more urgent as Amazon systematically tightens its receiving standards. Recent updates across Amazon's fulfillment network include:


-


Updated advance ship notice (ASN / EDI 856) labeling protocols


-


Reduced error tolerance at receiving docks


-


Automated financial penalties under the Ships in Product Packaging (SIPP) framework


For non-compliant items, per-unit chargebacks can instantly transform profitable[purchase orders (POs)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-purchase-order) into net losses. Understanding how to align physical packaging with digital data streams is essential for any brand navigating Amazon's supply chain.


## Navigating the 1P vs. 3P Fulfillment Divide


Before configuring a single shipping carton, suppliers must distinguish between Amazon's two primary selling channels:[Vendor Central (1P)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/a-users-guide-to-vendor-central) and Seller Central / Fulfillment by Amazon (3P). Conflating these fulfillment models is one of the fastest ways to generate systemic compliance errors.[Each program](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-seller-central-vs-vendor-central) operates under a distinct set of operational rules, labeling standards, and penalty structures.


### First-Party (1P) Vendor Central Requirements


In the Vendor Central model, Amazon acts as a wholesale buyer, issuing POs directly to suppliers. Products are delivered to Amazon distribution centers (DCs) or fulfillment hubs in bulk. 1P compliance focuses heavily on logistics, transportation scheduling, and automated data exchange:


-


**Routing & scheduling:** Collect shipments must be booked through Transportation Central and scheduled via the Carrier Appointment Request Portal (CARP) within the confirmed PO delivery windows.


-


**Outer labeling:** Master cartons require[GS1-128 barcodes](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/gs1-standards-for-new-suppliers-gtins-upcs-and-case-codes) detailing PO numbers, ASINs, and exact unit counts. Pallets require unique Serial Shipping Container Codes (SSCC) on adjacent sides.


-


**Digital alignment:** Every shipment requires an electronic[ASN (EDI 856)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) transmitted after carrier departure but prior to warehouse arrival. Discrepancies between physical carton contents and the electronic ASN trigger receiving chargebacks and shortage deductions.


### Third-Party (3P) Seller Central / FBA Requirements


In the Seller Central model, brands sell directly to end consumers, utilizing Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) for warehousing and customer delivery. FBA compliance centers on individual item prep, unit identification, and parcel network survival:


-


**Unit barcodes:** Every unit requires an accessible, scannable barcode. Sellers opt into Fulfillment Network[SKUs](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-stock-keeping-unit-sku) (FNSKUs) to assign unique identifiers tied to their seller account, preventing inventory commingling.


-


**Container prep:** Individual units must be fully prepped, six-sided, and properly sealed prior to arrival. Amazon charges per-unit prep fees if warehouse staff must add polybags or bubble wrap to uncertified inventory.


-


**Carton restrictions:** Standard shipping cartons sent to FBA must not exceed 25 inches on any side or weigh more than 50 pounds unless containing a single oversized unit.


## Labeling and Prep Failure Points That Drain Margins


Small errors during packing and labeling account for a large portion of Amazon chargebacks. Systematically addressing common failure points on the warehouse floor allows suppliers to eliminate preventable fees.


### Barcode Visibility and Accuracy


Unscannable or misplaced barcodes disrupt automated sorting belts, forcing warehouse personnel to handle cartons manually. OnFBA shipments , failure to cover legacy manufacturer barcodes or existing carton markings leads to scanning errors and misrouted inventory. Master cartons require a clean, high-quality barcode placed at least two centimeters away from box edges and tape seams.


### Outer Carton and Cushioning Specifications


Amazon enforces strict structural standards for shipping containers. Master boxes must consist of slotted or corrugated cardboard rated for edge crush strength. Loose items are prohibited.


For internal cushioning, suppliers must use approved materials such as bubble wrap, air pillows, polyethylene foam, or full sheets of paper. Disallowed materials — including styrofoam, packing peanuts, shredded paper, and crinkle wrap — result in shipment flags or dock rejections. Cartons weighing between 50 and 99 pounds require clear Team Lift labels, while shipments exceeding 100 pounds require Mech Lift labels.


### Polybag and Safety Mandates


Polybags used for primary or inner packaging must meet a minimum thickness of 1.5 mils (0.001 inches) and remain completely transparent, except when packaging adult merchandise. Any polybag with an opening of 5 inches or larger (measured flat) must display a legible suffocation warning. The warning must be printed directly on the bag or applied as a prominent label with font sizes scaled to the bag's dimensions. Polybags cannot protrude more than 3 inches past the product's physical dimensions.

## Category-Specific Prep Standards


Certain product categories carry mandatory prep protocols:


-


**Sold-as-set items:** Multi-packs must be physically sealed together inside a single package. The exterior must display a clear label stating "Sold as Set, Do Not Separate," covering any individual unit barcodes.


-


**Fragile goods:** Glass, ceramics, liquids, and delicate items must be wrapped securely in bubble wrap and pass a 3-foot drop test without breaking or leaking.


-


**Perishable items:** Products with expiration dates must feature the date formatted as MM-DD-YYYY or MM-YYYY printed on both the master carton and individual units in 36-point font or larger.


## The ASN and Document Trail: Where Shortages Become Disputes


For Vendor Central suppliers, the ASN (EDI 856) represents the critical link between physical fulfillment and financial settlement. When Amazon receives a shipment, automated scanners reconcile the physical carton count against the digital ASN.


If a discrepancy occurs due to inaccurate case counts, missing carton-level details, or late transmission, Amazon's system flags a shortage claim or an ASN mismatch chargeback. Shortage claims directly deduct the value of alleged missing units from invoice payments. Receiving delays and documentation gaps frequently trigger false shortage claims on fully delivered shipments.


[Winning a chargeback or shortage dispute](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/unlock-your/how-to-win-your-amazon-disputes) requires a complete documentation trail. Suppliers who rely solely on carrier tracking numbers often lose disputes because a tracking scan does not prove carton contents. Operations teams must maintain a centralized order file containing:


1.


The original PO (EDI 850)


1.


The exact EDI 856 ASN transmission confirmation log


1.


The stamped[bill of lading (BOL / EDI 211)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/bill-lading-bol-supplypike) or signed[proof of delivery (POD / EDI 861)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-proof-of-delivery) detailing piece counts


1.


Date-stamped pre-shipment photographs of loaded pallets and scannable GS1 carton labels


Presenting this matching evidence within the dispute window is the only reliable path to financial recovery.


**Related Reading** :[ASN Submission and Labeling Workflow at Amazon](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/asn-submission-and-labeling-workflow)


## Strategic Packaging Redesign: SIPP and Frustration-Free Packaging


Beyond operational compliance, Amazon provides a strategic pathway for high-volume brand owners to lower fulfillment costs through its[Ships in Product Packaging (SIPP)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/amazon-sipp-requirements-explained) program, formerly known as Frustration-Free Packaging (FFP).


The SIPP initiative categorizes packaging into three tiers:


-


**Tier 1 (frustration-free packaging):** Requires rigid packaging that ships in its own container without an Amazon overbox, opens in under 120 seconds, achieves a box-utilization score above 30% (50% for fragile items), and consists entirely of 100% curbside recyclable materials.


-


**Tier 2 (ships in own container / SIOC):** Requires product packaging to withstand parcel delivery and ship safely without extra Amazon packaging but permits non-curbside recyclable components.


-


**Tier 3 (prep-free packaging / PFP):** Applies to smaller, sortable goods that cannot ship in their own packaging. Requires primary packaging that protects the item so Amazon workers can place it directly into an overbox without adding prep materials.


Certified items avoid non-compliance chargebacks, which stand at $1.99 per unit for non-certified standard and oversized ASINs. SIPP certified products shipped through FBA also qualify for fulfillment fee discounts, while right-sizing packaging reduces raw material spend and freight costs. Non-fragile packages under 50 pounds can undergo self-testing using ISTA 6-Amazon drop test protocols, while fragile goods must pass official[ISTA 6](https://ista.org/docs/6AmazoncomSIOCOverview.pdf) lab testing.


## Building a Repeatable Compliance Workflow


Achieving long-term compliance on Amazon requires converting guidelines into standardized operational procedures. Operations managers should establish a four-part verification checklist before releasing orders to the dock:


1.


**Pre-print audit:** Verify that barcode formatting,[GTIN](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/gs1-standards-for-new-suppliers-gtins-upcs-and-case-codes) assignments, and item descriptions match current Amazon catalog data exactly before printing carton labels.


1.


**Prep station SOPs:** Standardize category-specific prep steps, ensuring polybag suffocation warnings, sold-as-set stickers, and expiration dates are applied consistently.


1.


**Dock verification scans:** Scan external carton barcodes on finished pallets to confirm legibility and verify that old or conflicting barcodes are completely covered.


1.


**Automated ASN generation:** Ensure electronic ASNs are generated directly from scanned carton data and transmitted immediately upon truck dispatch.


By embedding these checkpoints into daily warehouse operations, suppliers transform compliance from an unpredictable cost center into a reliable driver of supply chain efficiency.
